sections.heading: What is inversion?
sections.body: Inversion means putting the verb (or auxiliary) before the subject. It is used in formal English for emphasis, especially after negative or limiting adverbs at the beginning of a sentence.

sections.heading: Inversion after negative adverbs
table: Never have I seen such a beautiful place.
Not only did she arrive late, but she also forgot the tickets.
Hardly had I arrived when the phone rang.
No sooner had we left than it started raining.
Little did he know what was going to happen.

sections.heading: Inversion after 'only'
table: Only when you try will you succeed.
Only after the meeting did I understand.
Only if you study will you pass.
Only then did I realise my mistake.

sections.heading: Cleft sentences
sections.body: Cleft sentences split a sentence into two parts to emphasise one element.
table: What I need is a holiday.
The reason I left was the noise.

sections.heading: Other emphatic structures
list: So + adjective + be + subject: So tired was he that he fell asleep at once.
Such + be + noun: Such was his anger that he could not speak.
Do / does / did for emphasis: I do like your new haircut!

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not invert in normal affirmative sentences: 'Never I have seen' is wrong.
After 'not only' at the beginning, invert the main clause.
After 'It is/was' in a cleft sentence, use 'that' or 'who', not 'what'.

list.definition: Never have I seen such a mess.
Hardly had I arrived when it started raining.
No sooner had she left than he called.
Little did she know the truth.
Not only is he rich, but he is also generous.
Such was her surprise that she couldn't speak.
So tired was he that he fell asleep.
Not until midnight did they finish.
At no time did he lose his calm.
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
It was in 2020 that we met.
It is Maria who makes the decisions.
What I need is a break.
The reason why I left was the noise.
The thing is, I don't have time.
All I want is some peace.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: Never have I seen such a beautiful place.
Not only did she arrive late, but she also forgot the tickets.
Rarely does he complain about anything.
Only when you try will you succeed.
What I need is a holiday.
So tired was he that he fell asleep at once.
Little did she know the truth.
questions: In sentences 1 and 3, what happens to the word order after the negative adverb?
In sentence 2, why is the auxiliary 'did' used before the subject?
In sentence 4, what is the effect of starting with 'Only when'?
In sentences 5 and 6, what is being emphasised?
In sentence 7, why is 'was' placed before the subject?
In sentence 8, what does 'Little did she know' mean?

questions.prompt: Never ___ such a difficult exam.
questions.explanation: After Never at the start, we invert subject and auxiliary.

questions.prompt: It ___ my sister who told me the news.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentence: It + be + noun + who/that.

questions.prompt: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
questions.explanation: After 'Not only' at the start, invert the subject and verb.

questions.prompt: What I need ___ a holiday.
Only after the meeting ___ I understand the situation.
Rarely ___ arrive late.
Hardly ___ arrived when the phone rang.
It was in 2020 ___ we met.
Such ___ her surprise that she couldn't speak.
Little ___ he know what was coming.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 sentences starting with Never, Rarely, Not only, Only when, Little to add emphasis.
Rewrite 5 normal sentences as cleft sentences (It was... who/that; What I... is...).
Write an emphatic paragraph about a dramatic event using at least 4 inversions or cleft structures.

questions.prompt: Never ___ I heard such a story.
questions.explanation: Inversion after Never with present perfect: have I heard.

questions.prompt: It ___ my brother who broke the window.
Not only ___ she sing, but she also dances.
questions.explanation: Inversion after Not only with modal: can she sing.

questions.prompt: What I want ___ some peace and quiet.
Only then ___ I realise my mistake.
Rarely ___ such a talented singer.
Hardly ___ started when it began to rain.
It was yesterday ___ I saw her.
So tired ___ he that he fell asleep immediately.
Little ___ she know the surprise waiting for her.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Inversion after negative adverbs: Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, No sooner, Little.
Inversion after 'Only when / after / if / then'.
Inversion after 'Not only' at the beginning of a sentence.
Cleft sentences: It + be + element + that/who.
Wh-cleft: What + clause + be + element.
So + adjective + be + subject. Such + be + noun.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not invert in normal affirmative sentences.
After 'Not only' at the beginning, invert the main clause.
After 'It is/was' in a cleft sentence, use 'that' or 'who', not 'what'.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: Never have I...
Not only... but also...
Only when... will...
It was... that...
What I need is...
So + adj + was + subject + that...
